text: So, if we were to do the same, then the next generation – because fiscal needs will continue to grow – they will have to face a greater tax burden, not to mention having fewer resources to cope with crisis, emergencies or anything that can emerge in this uncertain world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And not to mention that we have not even talked about the more than $50 billion which we have drawn from past reserves so far, for which we are very unlikely for now, to be able to pay back.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If we need revenues, we find revenues in other ways that we can do, whether through the GST increase or through other revenue raising sources.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The second point I would say is in fact, the disagreement on philosophy, is not just on reserves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because as Mr Murali Pillai has highlighted, WP has consistently, time and again, throughout Singapore's history, basically, opposed the GST increase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is not just a philosophical matter about the reserves.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is also a philosophical matter about the GST.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: You fundamentally oppose the GST increase, for whatever reasons, I cannot quite fathom, because the way that we have designed the GST in Singapore is very different.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have explained this repeatedly, it does not hurt the poor, it is fair, it is effective, it is a unique system.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And yet, WP continues to oppose GST and the GST increase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why I surmise, the only reason you might do so, is because of a political reason, because you know this is unpopular, and therefore, it serves your political interests to oppose GST.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, on the macro inflation risk and the practicalities on tackling profiteering, this is not something we talk about in theory, because we have had experience doing this, through repeated rounds of doing GST increases in previous years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Committee Against Profiteering, each time we stand it up, has proven to be effective, has proven to be able to effectively deter any businesses from profiteering and when we catch someone, we have been able to take very quick action.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have confidence in doing these sorts of things, not because of theory, but because of practical experience gained from past rounds of GST increases.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I would just like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister if he could respond to my third clarification on healthcare expenses and the urgency of introducing GST to meet healthcare expenditure in the next few years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have already talked about the projections for healthcare in 2010.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is a projection that we are able to make on account of our ageing population.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because, remember, the elderly on a per capita spend basis incurs more healthcare spending than the young.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Most of our healthcare spending is incurred when we get older, not when we are young.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Just the simple mathematics of it, as our population pyramid shifts to an older population, on that simple mathematics, healthcare spending must surely go up.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why, we have good basis and good confidence to project in the longer term, where the trends are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The only way in which we can avoid that, is somehow magically, we have older folks spending less on healthcare.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not know how that might even happen.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I hope Healthier SG will pay some dividends but let us be realistic.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even if it helps to slow things down, I think the fact that older folks will incur more healthcare spending, I think that is not going to go away.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The only other way to address this again, is, again, if we are honest, let us not spend so much for the elderly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I am sure, no one in this House wants to take such a position.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That structural increase is very clear, but on a year-to-year basis, next year, two years' time, how much more will healthcare spending go up, it is not so clear.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Because there will be some lumpy investments, there may be a new hospital here; maybe for pandemic reasons, we need to enhance our infection controls.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The question is, "That the Bill be now read a Second time".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As many as are of that opinion, say "Aye".
